conventions.convention: Assume full AC; use a nonempty oriented link, positive normal-disk meridians, full meridian abelianization, and only an explicitly declared epimorphism to a positive-rank free abelian deck group.
Coefficient vectors are rows with right action v·g = vρ(g)ψ(g); differentials act on the right. The Fox matrix has relator block rows and generator block columns.
Acyclic torsion uses determinant exponents (-1)^(i+1) and is taken modulo the exact subgroup {±det(ρ(g))ψ(g)^d : g ∈ G}; nonacyclic fraction-field torsion is defined as zero.

A Wada column is admissible only when its entire boundary-block determinant is nonzero. Exterior interpretation requires a supplied based simple-spine certificate, not merely a presentation of the same group.

The positive Artin generator sends x_i to x_i x_(i+1) x_i^(-1) and x_(i+1) to x_i. Burau blocks use cumulative meridians g_i = x_1⋯x_i; the axis meridian acts trivially, and the designated denominator is det(ρ(g_n)ψ(g_n) − I).

load_bearing.statement: Defines the twisted cellular complex using the right coefficient action, its fraction-field localization, zero torsion for nonacyclic complexes, and the alternating determinant torsion modulo the exact determinant/deck-unit subgroup for acyclic complexes.

For the based presentation 2-complex and the stated row-coefficient convention, the evaluated Fox-Jacobian blocks are exactly its twisted cellular boundary blocks; the degree-one boundary blocks are ρ(x_j)ψ(x_j) − I.

For a connected finite based two-dimensional CW complex with one vertex, n ≥ 2 edges and n − 1 two-cells, a positive-rank free abelian deck epimorphism, and a field-valued representation, torsion degree-one homology over the Laurent ring implies acyclicity over its fraction field.

For the acyclic based twisted complex, changing cell lifts or orientations, or performing the specified elementary simple expansions and collapses, changes torsion only by an element of {±det(α(g)) : g ∈ G}.

For a certified based deficiency-one exterior spine, positive-rank deck epimorphism, torsion degree-one Laurent-ring homology and an admissible column, the localized complex is acyclic, the deleted Fox minor is nonzero, and its quotient by the selected boundary determinant represents torsion. Every admissible column gives the same class.

Under the stated compatible based closure-spine, axis-spine and filling certificates, coefficient extension and D ≠ 0, exterior torsion is represented by N/D on the acyclic branch; on the nonacyclic branch N = 0 and torsion is zero.

concerns.concern: Fact F9 says the solid-torus comparison is 'additionally computed in step 2.3', but there is no step 2.3. The comparison is computed in step 3.1.

Step 1.1 says, 'Give X its natural finite CW structure with one vertex, core edges a,b,c, and 2-cells λ₂,λ₃'. Here X was defined as the union of two mapping cylinders: the common source circle c and the two target core circles are disjoint, so that actual space cannot have the asserted one-vertex structure with all three as core edges. The usual construction first includes the two connecting cylinder edges and then collapses their maximal tree to obtain the asserted presentation complex. That finite simple comparison is omitted from the claimed spine certificate.

seams_checked.note: The batch does not infer an exterior spine from a Wirtinger group presentation. Its Wada and Burau interfaces explicitly require geometric simple-spine certificates.
Compact exteriors retain their boundary, positive meridians use the normal-disk convention, and the knot meridian generates abelianization. Full AC covers the supplier's countable-choice assumption.

The compact/open exterior comparison preserves positive-meridian deck variables. Coloring is an explicit quotient of full abelianization; no claim that arbitrary specialization preserves homology or acyclicity is used.

The direct use in def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures concerns finite twisted chains, group rings and full AC. It does not invoke the Laurent-field Wada theorem for noncommutative or von Neumann coefficients.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its current item inventory contains no direct dependency or citation to an assigned batch-65 item. No stronger torsion assertion was found along this page edge.

Adjoint homology is separately defined through intrinsic local coefficients without a positive-rank deck requirement. The rationality argument uses a separate presentation-homology supplier and does not infer a simple exterior spine or apply the acyclic Wada theorem to untwisted adjoint homology.
